A1.justification: Both PDFs describe AdAEM and retain matching core methods, experiments and results. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial additions and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark construction, evaluations of 16 LLMs, human judgments, controlled value-priming experiments and reliability analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds Moral Foundations evaluations, GPT-5 priming, approximation validation and robustness experiments.

M1.justification: The core exploration/refinement procedure, opinion extraction and TrueSkill aggregation remain. However, v2's Ethics Statement reports integrating Llama-Guard-4-12B into the released iterative process to screen questions and responses and discard harmful questions, adding a procedural safeguard.

E1.justification: v2 adds actual evaluation under Moral Foundations Theory, previously discussed only as a possible extension. Appendix J constructs AdAEM Bench-MFT with 589 questions covering five moral foundations, substantially extending the evaluation targets beyond the retained Schwartz-value benchmark.

E2.justification: The original SVS, ValueBench and ValueDCG comparison remains. v2 adds Moral Foundations Questionnaire as an evaluated comparator in Tables 14–15 and introduces ValueBench into the controlled-priming validation in Table 11.

E3.justification: The human study changes from 50 question pairs and two annotators to 300 pairs and five annotators. New protocols include a 100-seed-question approximation comparison, alternative model configurations, 200/500/1000-question evaluations, and a separately specified MFT construction budget and model pool.

E4.justification: v2 adds independent priming checks using ValueBench and GPT-5, approximate-versus-probability-based reward validation, sensitivity to participating models and question counts, explicit failure cases, and another convergence experiment. These examine validity and sensitivity questions beyond v1's existing topic, temporal, regional and five-partition analyses.

E5.justification: v2 extends statistical agreement assessment with Pearson correlation and intraclass correlation estimation for implementation, model-configuration and subset comparisons. Existing paired t-tests, effect sizes, Cohen's kappa and five-partition reliability reporting remain; no new seed counts, repeated-run counts or confidence intervals are specified.

E6.justification: The original 16-model scores and o3-mini priming table remain unchanged, but substantial new MFT, priming and robustness results appear. Table 9 replaces human value-elicitation scores of 1.87/2.46 with 1.47/2.24 for general/AdAEM questions under the expanded study, so this is not a same-setting performance improvement.

T1.justification: Most derivations are retained from v1 Appendix C in v2 Appendix D. v2 adds entropy-bound reasoning in Appendix I.1 and a claimed IM convergence justification in E.6. Equation (1) also presents as an equality the transition previously described as a lower-bound substitution.

C1.justification: The central claim of dynamic, self-extensible evaluation that exposes LLM value differences remains. Cross-value-system construction changes from future work in v1's conclusion to an achieved contribution in v2, while the introduction generalizes the dataset contribution beyond its original Schwartz-specific description.

C2.justification: New discussions operationalize LLM values as latent behavioral variables and distinguish inherent preferences from user-induced steering and context sensitivity. Appendix C.7 distinguishes factual memorization from value contamination and explains comparability within shared question sets. Failure-case analysis adds substantive explanations of unsuccessful question generation.

D1.justification: v2 provides a public repository address and states code/data release, whereas v1 mentions submission attachments. It adds detailed probability-based reward calculations, settings for new experiments, model-selection rationale, safeguard implementation, and annotator recruitment, consent, compensation and time accounting.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands literature-supported positioning around latent value representations, value/persona steering, moral-foundation evaluation and approximation/convergence. Additions include Cahyawijaya et al. (2024), Jin et al. (2025) and Agakov (2005). The original distinction from static value benchmarks remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, contributions and methodological exposition undergo broad rewriting and terminology clarification. Appendices are reorganized, limitations move into Appendix H, and the NeurIPS checklist is replaced by a different reporting structure including reproducibility and LLM-usage statements. Author information and citation style also change.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is substantially redrawn, the notation table expands, and Tables 11–18 and Figures 18–21 introduce new displays. Existing figures are resized or relocated, including the temporal-distribution plot moving to the appendix, alongside extensive conference-template reformatting.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation of previously untested generality and sensitivity through MFT evaluation, independent priming checks, approximation comparisons and model/question-count robustness tests. Expanded human evaluation and implementation disclosures also improve scrutiny. The new convergence guarantee remains insufficiently established for the heuristic implementation, but this qualification does not outweigh the stronger empirical foundation.
